questions.prompt: Why did many FLOP-reducing approximate attention methods fail to run faster?
options: Attention was bound by memory traffic, not FLOPs, and they didn't reduce the traffic
questions.explanation: The wrong model of the machine: count bytes, not FLOPs.

questions.prompt: What does FlashAttention store for the backward pass instead of the N×N probabilities?
options: Per-row softmax statistics (max and sum), recomputing scores block by block
questions.explanation: Recomputation trades FLOPs for memory traffic and wins.

questions.prompt: Which FlashAttention-2 change targets the tail effect from Chapter 5.4?
options: Parallelising over sequence length, so one long sequence with few heads still fills the GPU
questions.explanation: More, smaller work units when batch × heads is small.

questions.prompt: Why does FlashAttention-3 overlap softmax of one warpgroup with GEMMs of another?
options: Exponentials run on far slower units than tensor cores, so serialising them would leave tensor cores idle
questions.explanation: Hide the slow non-matmul work behind the fast matmuls.
